constraints: Maintainer process constraint: the issue states the maintainers are implementing this in-house and external pull requests for it will be closed; the approach is therefore a recommendation for the maintainers, not a PR plan for an outside contributor.

parser.rs QUERY_CACHE is built from crate::lang::supported_languages(); a name missing from that list returns ParserError::UnsupportedLanguage, so 'php' must be added there (note: 'css' is in EXTENSION_MAP but not in supported_languages()).

Symbol matching in defuse compares capture node text to the symbol name (parser_elements.rs ~873); PHP variable_name text includes the leading '$', so the query must capture the inner name node to match a symbol like 'z'.
Use LANGUAGE_PHP (mixed HTML and PHP mode) rather than LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, because the issue requires zero ERROR nodes for files that mix HTML and <?php ... ?>.
Workspace lints deny unwrap_used and expect_used outside test code; handlers must use Option/bounds-checked slicing, as java.rs does.

Dependency age gate: new Cargo.lock entries must be at least 7 days old. tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 is listed on GitHub as published 2026-11-19 (8 days before this run's 2026-11-27 date); 0.25.1 was published 2026-10-06 and is the fallback.

Scope limits from the issue: no extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver or find_receiver_type; no trait use resolution, property or constant extraction, attributes, namespace alias resolution; no .phtml, .inc, .module or .php5 extensions; no tool handler or schema changes.
Parameter surface and tool schema must not change (AGENTS.md: the tool schema is the contract).
test_coverage: Every existing language handler has inline unit tests in its own file (queries_compile, element happy path, inheritance happy and edge, defuse write site; css.rs has three tests over a parse_and_query helper). languages/mod.rs has a table test covering remaining languages, lang.rs has extension-map tests (language_for_extension), and the core and MCP integration test files cover analyze_file per language. No test today asserts parity between EXTENSION_MAP languages and supported_languages() (grep of crates/*.rs shows only parser.rs:1057 using the length), which is consistent with the css gap going undetected. PHP will need coverage at all three levels.

approaches.name: A: Java-mirror full handler (recommended)
approaches.description: Add crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs with the five query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY over function_definition, method_declaration, class, interface, trait, enum; CALL_QUERY over function_call_expression, member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression; REFERENCE_QUERY over named_type; IMPORT_QUERY over namespace_use_declaration; DEFUSE_QUERY over parameters, assignments, updates and variable reads) plus extract_inheritance that walks base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Register 'php' in lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages), mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info with LANGUAGE_PHP, get_ts_language), root and crate Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, README. Add inline php.rs tests and one aptu-coder integration test.
pros: Matches the issue scope exactly (five constants, extract_inheritance, registry, tests)
Same shape as java.rs and swift.rs, so reviewers can diff it against known handlers
DEFUSE_QUERY gives analyze_symbol def-use sites for PHP, which the Java handler also provides
Uses the mixed-mode grammar, so HTML templates parse without ERROR nodes
cons: DEFUSE_QUERY on name nodes is coarser than the grammar allows, so it needs its own tests to avoid false positives on function names
Adds about eight files, including Cargo.lock churn and a README edit
Binary size grows with another grammar; the issue requires the delta to be reported

approaches.name: B: Minimal handler without DEFUSE and REFERENCE
approaches.description: Same registry wiring, but php.rs keeps only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and extract_inheritance, and sets defuse_query: None and reference_query: None in mod.rs, as css.rs and markdown do.
pros: Smallest change and the fewest query tests to maintain
Element, call, import and inheritance acceptance criteria can all be met
cons: Violates the issue Scope, which lists DEFUSE_QUERY among the five required constants
analyze_symbol def-use returns no sites for PHP (parser_elements.rs ~850 returns empty when compiled.defuse is None)
Leaves the handler inconsistent with the other OO languages

approaches.name: C: Strip HTML and use the PHP-only grammar
approaches.description: Use LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY and pre-process source to blank out non-PHP ranges (keeping byte offsets), so the query set can stay as in A but the grammar never sees HTML text nodes.
pros: PHP-only grammar has fewer node kinds, so queries are simpler
Byte offsets stay valid for line numbers
cons: Requires a new preprocessing step outside the handler contract (parse path in parser.rs changes)
Must detect <?php and ?> boundaries correctly, including short tags and ?>-terminated comments
More risk and code than A for the same acceptance criteria; the issue explicitly asks for zero ERROR nodes on mixed files, which A satisfies natively

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets all five query constants and the extract_inheritance contract in the issue, and it follows java.rs and swift.rs one-to-one. Use LANGUAGE_PHP (mixed mode) so HTML templates produce no ERROR nodes. Pin tree-sitter-php at 0.25.2, which passes the 7-day age gate; fall back to 0.25.1 if cargo deny rejects it. Capture the inner name nodes in DEFUSE_QUERY so symbol text matches without '$'. Add 'php' to supported_languages() in lang.rs; without it QUERY_CACHE rejects php. Verify every query with a compile test before wiring, as the issue suggests, because this run did not compile anything.

inheritance_walk_citation:
Source inspected: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php, path php/src/grammar.json and php/src/node-types.json, read via gh api contents (php/grammar.js only calls defineGrammar('php') from common/define-grammar.js, so the rules are in grammar.json).

Literal grammar.json rules (verbatim JSON from php/src/grammar.json):
{"class_declaration": {"type": "PREC_RIGHT", "value": 0, "content": {"type": "SEQ", "members": [{"type": "CHOICE", "members": [{"type": "FIELD", "name": "attributes", "content": {"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "attribute_list"}}, {"type": "BLANK"}]}, {"type": "REPEAT", "content": {"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "_modifier"}}, {"type": "ALIAS", "content": {"type": "PATTERN", "value": "class", "flags": "i"}, "named": false, "value": "class"}, {"type": "FIELD", "name": "name", "content": {"type": "RESERVED", "content": {"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "name"}, "context_name": "classes"}}, {"type": "CHOICE", "members": [{"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "base_clause"}, {"type": "BLANK"}]}, {"type": "CHOICE", "members": [{"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "class_interface_clause"}, {"type": "BLANK"}]}, {"type": "FIELD", "name": "body", "content": {"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "declaration_list"}}]}}}
{"base_clause": {"type": "SEQ", "members": [{"type": "ALIAS", "content": {"type": "PATTERN", "value": "extends", "flags": "i"}, "named": false, "value": "extends"}, {"type": "SEQ", "members": [{"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "_name"}, {"type": "REPEAT", "content": {"type": "SEQ", "members": [{"type": "STRING", "value": ","}, {"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "_name"}]}}]}]}}
{"class_interface_clause": {"type": "SEQ", "members": [{"type": "ALIAS", "content": {"type": "PATTERN", "value": "implements", "flags": "i"}, "named": false, "value": "implements"}, {"type": "SEQ", "members": [{"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "_name"}, {"type": "REPEAT", "content": {"type": "SEQ", "members": [{"type": "STRING", "value": ","}, {"type": "SYMBOL", "name": "_name"}]}}]}]}}

Literal node-types.json entry for class_declaration: fields = {"attributes": {"multiple": false, "required": false, "types": [{"type": "attribute_list", "named": true}]}, "body": {"multiple": false, "required": true, "types": [{"type": "declaration_list", "named": true}]}, "name": {"multiple": false, "required": true, "types": [{"type": "name", "named": true}]}}; children types = ["abstract_modifier", "base_clause", "class_interface_clause", "final_modifier", "readonly_modifier", "static_modifier", "var_modifier", "visibility_modifier"].

Field walk, class declaration to extends and implements names:
1. Start at the class_declaration node. child_by_field_name("name") returns the class's own name (grammar: field(name, RESERVED name)). Field body returns the declaration_list.
2. The extends clause is NOT a field. Grammar: choice(base_clause | BLANK) is an unfielded child. Iterate the node's children and select child.kind() == "base_clause".
3. The implements clause is NOT a field either. Grammar: choice(class_interface_clause | BLANK) is an unfielded child. Select child.kind() == "class_interface_clause".
4. Inside base_clause, the named children are name | qualified_name | relative_name (grammar: seq(ALIAS(extends), seq(_name, REPEAT(seq(',', _name))))). Each named child becomes "extends {source text}". The grammar's list form is shared with interfaces, so do not assume a single base for a class.
5. Inside class_interface_clause, the named children are the same kinds (grammar: seq(ALIAS(implements), seq(_name, REPEAT(seq(',', _name))))). Each becomes "implements {source text}".
6. There are no superclass or interfaces fields, unlike java.rs, which calls child_by_field_name("superclass") and child_by_field_name("interfaces"). Mirror swift.rs (child iteration) instead.
7. interface_declaration uses base_clause for its parents, so extends should be emitted there too; trait_declaration has neither clause; enum_declaration uses class_interface_clause for implements and a primitive_type child for the backing type (':' string | int).
8. Qualified names keep their leading backslash in the source text, e.g. "extends \\App\\Models\\Model". Decide whether to keep or strip it; the issue's example uses plain names.
